::: {#rem-why-warmup}

#### Why warm up

At the start of training the [parameters](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-parameter) are far from good ones,
and the [gradients](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/linear-regression.html#def-gradient) can be large,
so a [learning rate](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-learning-rate) that works later can throw the network into a bad region in the first few steps.
@goyal2017accurate proposed gradual [warmup](#def-warmup)
for training with very large minibatches.
For [Adam](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-adam),
its running average of squared gradients rests on only a few gradients at first,
so its step sizes vary widely,
and warmup keeps those early steps small [@liu2020variance].

:::
